figures.finding: Antarctica has no actors' agreement, guild or fund of its own: no state's sovereignty over it is recognised under the Antarctic Treaty, and visits (filming among them) fall under the Treaty parties' rules for non-governmental activities.
figures.applies: Antarctica (AQ), as of 2026-11-01; who engages a performer or crew there, and on what terms, follows the production's own country (not modeled).

sources.said: Antarctica shall be used for peaceful purposes only Art. I … No acts or activities taking place while the present Treaty is in force shall constitute a basis for asserting, supporting or denying a claim to territorial sovereignty in Antarctica or create any rights of sovereignty in Antarctica.

The main ATCM regulations and guidelines for tourists and expedition organizers are compiled in the Manual of Regulations and Guidelines Relevant to Tourism and Non-Governmental Activities in the Antarctic Treaty area

figures.finding: No language is set for screen work in Antarctica; the Antarctic Treaty itself is authentic in English, French, Russian and Spanish.

value.basis: the Treaty's authentic texts, not a statement on film

blockers.sought: The stage actor's minimum: an agreement, a rate card or a statutory rule setting a stage actor's pay, or a source saying none does.

tried.institution: Antarctic Treaty Secretariat: https://www.ats.aq/e/antarctictreaty.html (saved files/m10/aq-ats-treaty.html, sha256 865237a938be88ecd652c08b01701d49fa9c8dfc99903fe3c17a17e7aecc1e94) and its searchable text https://documents.ats.aq/recatt/att005_e.pdf (files/m10/aq-att005_e.pdf, sha256 5d6852c0910a9f51e8205b1513567f2e13e9b6a04618fbabec753c258a445ebe), read whole (items 8, 9) [same attempt as item 8] (the stage actor's minimum, the methods round of 2026-11-04). Result: No sovereignty recognised (Art. IV: 'No acts or activities taking place while the present Treaty is in force shall constitute a basis for asserting, supporting or denying a claim to territorial sovereignty in Antarctica'); Art. VIII: observers and scientific personnel 'shall be subject only to the jurisdiction of the Contracting Party of which they are nationals', 'without prejudice to the respective positions of the Contracting Parties relating to jurisdiction over all other persons in Antarctica'. No body or rule for theatre, playwrights' or actors' pay: a play made by people in Antarctica falls under their own state's law and agreements (not modeled).
tried.official-register: United Nations Treaty Series vol. 402, No. 5778, The Antarctic Treaty (registered by the United States, 4 August 1961): https://treaties.un.org/doc/Publication/UNTS/Volume%20402/volume-402-I-5778-English.pdf (files/m10/aq-unts402.pdf, sha256 b6f66ee824a3688a995042f13698662c01b32153768115ff159fb24d7f38b3b6), English text read (items 8, 9) [same attempt as item 8] (the stage actor's minimum, the methods round of 2026-11-04). Result: Read: Art. IV (no territorial sovereignty asserted or created) and Art. VIII (jurisdiction by nationality for observers and scientific personnel) as in the Secretariat's text; no labour, theatre or authors' provision. No state register of agreements exists for Antarctica.
tried.web-search: WebSearch (1 of 10, standard): 'Antarctica theatre play performed station actors playwright' (items 8, 9) [same attempt as item 8] (the stage actor's minimum, the methods round of 2026-11-04). Result: Plays set in Antarctica and staged elsewhere (Mat Smart's The Royal Society of Antarctica at The Gift Theatre, Chicago; Blowout Theatre Company, New York; The Fire on the Snow, ABC radio 1941), an expedition entertainment of 25 June 1902 on Ross Island (AusStage listing); no theatre company, agreement, playwright's or actor's pay in Antarctica.
tried.trade-press: Daily Herald, 22 Feb 2015, 'Naperville native's Antarctica journey inspires play' https://www.dailyherald.com/20150222/entertainment/naperville-natives-antarctica-journey-inspires-play/ (files/m10/aq-dailyherald-2015.html, sha256 990f63bd07f4d8f7fdef70df53792b4371cb13e5ee7a848f00b11e358f116284) read; AusStage event 115642 (files/m10/aq-ausstage-115642.html) fetched, its page body script-rendered (no text) (items 8, 9) [same attempt as item 8] (the stage actor's minimum, the methods round of 2026-11-04). Result: The playwright worked at McMurdo Station 'cleaning bathrooms and sweeping floors 10 hours a day, six days a week' and the play premiered at The Gift Theatre, Chicago: the playwriting and the run were under US terms, not Antarctic ones. No primary on pay quoted.
